dryEvidence: loam-hollow-rail, five rounds in fresh contexts, each told what earlier rounds found. Round 1: one confirmed (the forward-only case's first-pool half true by timing) and two plausible (the gather never read; the inbox-less resolver branch unrailed). Round 2: two confirmed (the per-person revoke's code burn unrailed; the forward-only rail one-sided). Round 3: four confirmed (per-key token count unpinned at both surfaces; a dead stale-handle branch with an overclaiming comment; the drop wrapper clearing the handle on a REFUSED drop; the pre-§58 pair through the panel unrailed). Round 4: one confirmed (the no-such-pair outcome unpinned) and three plausible (sibling naming one-sided; the ground strike unasserted; the sticky backend overclaiming at the bytes) — all folded as rails. Round 5: three confirmed rail gaps (the 503-on-failed-sibling path railable with a refusing backend, and the header's claim otherwise false; the drop-window guard unrailed; the unattached-row case's nothing-struck assertions not load-bearing at the plan step) — all folded as rails. Every finding folded; the final rails: twenty-one exchange cases and three ledger cases. Mechanical: diff-scoped against the S1a branch at 6110644 with nine killer suites: 17 mutants, 16 killed; the one survivor flips the type literal 'readonly othersPair?: true' to false, which the runtime never sees. Earlier runs earned two ledger rails for the grant command's --user path.

dryEvidence: loam-lens-name, three rounds in fresh contexts. Round 1: three confirmed (the new --user flag refused by the CLI's own parser; a uniqueness sentinel colliding with a legal username; the admin page's per-inbox revoke calling the connector-wide revoke). Round 2: two confirmed (revoke pages naming the whole connector for a pair's act; the live-token count keyed by client) and two plausible (a re-attached handle of a different kind; the user-less pair unnamable as a revoke target). Round 3: three confirmed (the sibling pools unnamed by 'every other connection is untouched'; the user-less branch keeping whole-connector copy; the ledger's per-connector count on per-key rows) and one plausible (a revoke scope one ?: from its opposite → a discriminated RevokeScope with a no-such-pair outcome). Every item folded; the last round found every value the right kind: every actor a public key, every actorSeed a seed, one JSON-pair uniqueness key, the inbox name computed by one function at both sites.

dryEvidence: loam-suppression, six rounds. Round 1: two confirmed (the per-inbox revoke dropping every person's key; the production inbox pool in-memory and never re-attached at boot, so a bound container refused after a restart) and one plausible (two homes for one delta on a re-bind, the window the next slice closes). Round 2: three confirmed (a one-person revoke leaving the same key's sibling pool with its write grant; the re-attached raw handle accepting detach and leaving a stale entry after drop; a re-consent after a drop binding to a struck inbox) and two plausible (the surviving-grant scanners counting any negation — pre-existing, unreachable today, named as a follow-on; an empty in-memory pool attached without a factory). Round 3: one confirmed (the refused-drop strand) and one plausible-low (the sibling strike gated on the row's own pool). Round 4: three confirmed edge cases the sibling logic opened (a row whose own pool is unattached reported struck; a failed sibling strike absent from a 200 page; the sibling list unfenced to the person's reach) and one plausible (the drop window between unregister and the handle's clearing) — all folded, with rails for the first and third and the fence. Round 5: one confirmed (the connector half unfenced: a person revoking a foreign key's inbox in their own reach retired the OTHER person's pair — fenced to the session's person, with a mirror rail) and one plausible (the sibling filter lacking the drop-window check — added). Round 6: nothing confirmed; three plausible — the pre-§58 arm revocable from any row that holds the key (intended per greenfield; named as a decision for Myk in the PR), the connections panel row disclosing another person's client and count where the pages withhold it (fenced: the row says only 'bound as another person's connector'), and the pre-existing 'does not rewrite history' sentence that dissolves when the next slice retires the store-wide grant (named as a follow-on). Cross-model: adlc review --providers gemini --base t262-bind-at-consent, APPROVE with no material adversarial findings at c6ba745, ab62e2a, 99de81b, 7d4b50f, 522f758, e6d773e, 1f6d9e6 and 6110644 (the final revision).
